title: Docs: Fix ESLint docs and broken links in the rules settings

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Clarify that deprecated webpack5 frameworks remain available as fallback options.**

The narrowing to Vite-based frameworks is aligned with current Storybook guidance, where @storybook/react-vite is recommended for most React projects since the Vite-based framework is faster, more modern, and offers better support for testing features. However, the documentation should clarify that webpack5-based frameworks (@storybook/react-webpack5) remain available for users who need specific Webpack features not available in Vite.

Consider adding a note that webpack5 alternatives are still documented and available for projects with special build tool requirements, preventing users from assuming these options have been completely removed.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/lib/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/no-renderer-packages.md around lines 15 to
21, the list of recommended Vite-based frameworks should be supplemented with a
brief note clarifying that webpack5-based frameworks (e.g.,
@storybook/react-webpack5, @storybook/server-webpack5) remain available as
documented fallback options for projects that require specific Webpack features;
add a single-sentence note directly after the Vite recommendations stating that
webpack5 alternatives are still maintained and documented for users with special
build-tool requirements so readers don't assume those options were removed.
```

</details>

<!-- fingerprinting:phantom:poseidon:puma -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment by CodeRabbit -->
comments.label_reasoning: The comment suggests the documentation is incomplete/misleading by not clarifying that webpack5 frameworks are still available, which could confuse users reading the docs.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests adding a note clarifying that webpack5-based frameworks remain available, implying a concrete documentation change.

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Update documentation to clarify ESLint version requirements for these imports.**

The `defineConfig` and `globalIgnores` imports from 'eslint/config' are valid for ESLint's flat config, but the code snippet lacks important version context. These helpers were introduced in ESLint v9.22.0. Since Storybook's ESLint plugin supports v8.57+, the documentation should clarify that users on older ESLint versions supporting flat config should import from @eslint/config-helpers instead of eslint/config.

Consider adding a note specifying the minimum ESLint version required or providing examples for both import paths (eslint/config for v9.22+ and @eslint/config-helpers for earlier versions).

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In docs/configure/integration/eslint-plugin.mdx around lines 43 to 48, the
snippet imports defineConfig and globalIgnores from 'eslint/config' without
specifying ESLint version constraints; update the documentation to state that
these helpers require ESLint v9.22.0 or newer and that users on older ESLint
versions that still support flat config (e.g., Storybook environments supporting
v8.57+) should instead import from @eslint/config-helpers; add a short note
indicating the minimum version (v9.22.0) and include two example import lines or
callouts showing the alternate import paths (eslint/config for v9.22+ and
@eslint/config-helpers for earlier versions).
```

</details>

comments.label_reasoning: The comment indicates the documentation lacks important version context/constraints for the ESLint imports shown, making the docs potentially misleading for users on different ESLint versions.
